gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and stencil-cut, its single-weight strokes opening wide in the c, e and s. Against Nulshock's stretched, spaced-out outline capitals, that crisp plain sans makes the strongest single quality a clean technical edge.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-radio-canada: Nulshock stretches its unshaded outline wide, with spacing so generous that the capitals barely rise above the lowercase beside them. It handles the loud announcing; Radio Canada keeps its tall, full c, s and z for the steady reading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-radio-canada-big: Nulshock stretches wide and bold, drawn with a steady unshaded outline. Radio Canada Big matches that steadiness with a monoline sans whose large x-height fills the line and whose terminals finish well clear of the stem.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-readex-pro: Nulshock spreads its technical, bold letters out wide, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Readex Pro takes over below as a plain sans with broad terminal gaps, and a long passage would flow in one unvarying weight from word to word.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-ruda: Approachable is the first word for Ruda, a wire-thin sans-serif with wide-mouthed rounds. Its sizable x-height carries a longer stretch of text smoothly, each monoline stroke easy on the eye while Nulshock stays up above, stretched and bold.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-saira: Saira reads clean and tidy, with a see-through gap in every s and rounded letters reaching high toward the top line. A longer passage would move quickly under Nulshock's constant-width pen line.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-sarpanch: Approachable describes Sarpanch, a plain sans with a clearly open e and a compact gap up to its ascenders. Nulshock's heading has no contrast between stems and joins, so the two sit together comfortably.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-savate: Bold, stretched and technical up top, true monoline Nulshock meets Savate, whose thin strokes are only slightly lighter than its thick ones. Savate's open curves and tall round o keep the text below lively.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Nulshock draws its tube-like, constant-width stroke wide and spaced out. Under it, Schibsted Grotesk is a plain sans with big open e and a shapes, so a longer passage feels welcoming, its terminals never closing in.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-sen: Nulshock is stretched and spaced, its outline unshaded and technical. Sen sits beneath as a plain sans with tall lowercase and curved strokes that end before turning inward, so the heading's width gets a modern counterpart.
